theme: Precision Time Measurement, Base-60 System & Duration

conceptual_foundation.introduction: Focuses on temporal awareness, short time interval precision using seconds, morning routine timing, school sprint races, and elapsed duration calculations.

core_concepts.explanation: Time measurement relies on a sexagesimal (base-60) system where 60 seconds make 1 minute, and 60 minutes make 1 hour.
Reading time accurately using Hour hand (short), Minute hand (long), and Second hand (thin fast-moving hand).
core_concepts.example: When the thin second hand completes 1 full revolution (60 small ticks), the minute hand advances by 1 tick mark.

core_concepts.explanation: Developing an internal sense of 60 seconds by counting or observing short activities (blinking, pulse rate, 50m sprint).
core_concepts.example: A 100-metre school sprint is measured in seconds (e.g., 15 seconds), not minutes.

core_concepts.explanation: Determining the total time interval between a starting time and an ending time across hours, minutes, and seconds.
core_concepts.example: From 08:35 PM to 05:00 AM next day: 08:35 PM + 25 min -> 09:00 PM; 09:00 PM + 8 hours -> 05:00 AM. Total elapsed time = 8 hours 25 minutes.

core_concepts.explanation: Converting standard 12-hour clock times with AM/PM indicators to 24-hour digital clock formats.
core_concepts.example: 08:35 PM = 20:35 hours; 05:00 AM = 05:00 hours; 12:00 Midnight = 00:00 hours.

key_formulas_and_rules: Elapsed Time = End Time - Start Time
real_world_applications: Sports race timing, train and flight schedule reading, cooking/baking timer management, pulse monitoring, and exam duration tracking.
